description: A chaotic drone: a forced, damped Duffing oscillator coupled to two banks of twenty-four resonant bandpass filters, whose summed output is the force fed back into the oscillator

params.text: Sets the forcing amount, 0 to 10; past about 2.5 the forcing sine entrains the chaos and the module locks into a static tone, so the lively range is roughly a half to two and a half
Sets the frequency coefficient of the forcing sine: slow surging drones at the bottom of its travel, growls and tones at the top
Sets the damping: high chokes the chaos, low lets it ring
Sets the internal time step, 0 to 10, which scales how fast the whole system runs and multiplies with tone to give the forcing frequency
Low-passes the chaotic state before it reaches the filters, 0 to 5; higher is darker and rounder, and it has no CV jack
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the knob above
Chooses which of twenty factory frequency sets the first filter bank uses; switching glides every filter to the new set
Chooses which of twenty factory frequency sets the second filter bank uses; switching glides every filter to the new set
Multiplies the frequency of all forty-eight filters together, a twentieth to twice
Sets the resonance of all forty-eight filters, 2.5 to 800
Scatters the filters away from their preset frequencies and Q at random, none at the bottom of its travel; the pattern is seeded per instance and saved with the patch
Sets the level of the first filter bank, 0 to 2
Sets the level of the second filter bank, 0 to 2
Drives the filter sum, 0 to 3.5; it is inside the feedback loop, so it changes how the system behaves rather than only how loud it is

Chooses how the chaotic state is distorted: hard clip, soft clip, atan folding, an atan approximation, a tanh approximation, or an exact atan; it shapes the feedback rather than adding fuzz on the end
Switches the two filter banks out, leaving the raw Duffing oscillator: bounded chaos with hard resets
Zeroes the chaotic state and lights it again with a short parameter kick, which reads as a percussive hit

inputs.text: Added to the drive knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the tone knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the damp knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the rate knob through the attenuverter beside it
Sweeps the first bank across all twenty sets, 0V to 10V
Sweeps the second bank across all twenty sets, 0V to 10V
Multiplies the filter frequencies, one volt per octave
Added to the first bank's gain knob
Added to the second bank's gain knob
A signal that replaces the internal forcing sine as soon as it is patched: drums come back as chaotic resonance and voices as metal
A rising edge zeroes the chaotic state and lights it again

outputs.text: The filter banks summed, DC blocked, about ±5V and hard limited at ±10V
The chaotic state itself after the distortion, clamped and DC blocked, as a free modulation source

notes: this plays itself. At power-on and at every reset the chaos is lit by a short parameter kick, so the module always wakes up making sound.
if it sounds dead, turn the two bank gains up. Below roughly a total of 1.5 between them the Duffing settles onto a fixed point and the module becomes a static drone.
turning tone or rate right down takes the forcing below audio rate and the system breathes instead, surging into screaming resonance and collapsing back.
below about 10Hz of forcing the collapses become long silences. That is a setting, not a fault.
menu: Distortion oversampling — 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x or 16x, which anti-aliases the distortion stage
Bank glide — how long a bank, pitch or resonance change takes to slide: 20 ms, 100 ms, 500 ms or 2 s
